newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Moody's says Australia's NSW outlook improves.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Moody's says Australia's NSW outlook improves.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday it has revised the outlook for the state of New South Wales (NSW) foreign currency debt rating to improving from stable to reflect the outlook of the country of Australia's foreign currency rating.

"Moody's revised the outlook for the state of New South Wales' foreign currency debt rating from stable to improving, to reflect the revision in the outlook of the country of Australia's foreign currency rating," Moody's said.

"The revision in outlook does not reflect a change in New South Wales' intrinsic credit fundamentals, but solely reflects the change in outlook of the country ceiling for Australia's foreign currency debt," the ratings agency said.
Moody's said in the same statement that there was an improving outlook for three other Australian states, Victoria, Western Australia and Queensland.

On Wednesday, Moody's said Australia would probably have to wait about 18 months before it considers boosting the country's international credit status. On Tuesday, Moody's said the outlook for Australia's Aa2 rating was positive.
New South Wales also has an Aa2 foreign currency rating and a AAA domestic currency rating.
Western Australia has a AAA domestic currency rating while Victoria has an AA1 rating. Each has an AA2 foreign currency rating.
